nodes.title: Lattices and bilattices
nodes.statement: For a complete discrete valuation ring R with fraction field K, uniformizer t and residue field k, a lattice in a finite-dimensional K-space V is a finite free R-submodule spanning V. A bilattice is (V,L1,L2); morphisms are K-linear maps preserving both lattices. Define decreasing trace filtration trFil^i(L1/tL1)=image((t^i L2)∩L1→L1/tL1). The elementary-divisor type is the multiset of a_j with L2=⊕R t^{a_j}e_j for a basis of L1.

proofSteps: Use elementary divisors over the complete DVR.
Define the intersection before taking its image; quotienting L2 alone gives the wrong trace filtration.
acceptance: Checks distinguish the filtration from the lattice and are invariant under a change of uniformizer.

nodes.title: Specialization dominance
nodes.statement: Write G=M⋉U over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. For a bilattice with Levi type [mu_M], let [mu] be its induced G-cocharacter class. In every representation rho, rho([mu]) is dominated by the actual vector-bilattice type, with equal determinant degree. Equality in one closed faithful representation is equivalent to goodness of type [mu]. This is a comparison of types, not semicontinuity of all non-reductive cells in families.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Conjugate the Levi lattice to standard form.
Order unipotent weight factors and use exterior-power lattice bounds for dominance.
Equality in a faithful representation forces the residual weight factors to be integral in the required coordinates.
acceptance: In the G_a extension, the Levi type is (0,0) while the actual GL_2 type is (1,−1); this fixes the dominance orientation.

nodes.title: Exactness criterion for goodness
nodes.statement: For a pointwise bilatticed G-torsor in characteristic zero, the following are equivalent: it is good; BB1 is an exact filtered G-functor; BB2 is an exact filtered G-functor. For good type [mu], these functors have types [mu^-1] and [mu]. The BB functors preserve tensor products and duals but are not exact on arbitrary bilattices.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: A good cocharacter double coset gives two split exact filtered tensor functors.
Conversely split an exact trace filtration by a cocharacter and pass to the reductive Levi quotient.
Use specialization dominance to compare the induced Levi type with every representation type. Exactness forces equality in a faithful representation, hence goodness.
Exchange the two lattices to obtain the second criterion.
acceptance: The G_a example fails exactness on its defining extension, rather than contradicting tensor compatibility.

nodes.title: Recovery from a filtration
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring, with fraction field K, algebraically closed residue field C and uniformizer t, with its coefficient field embedded compatibly in R. For a connected linear group G and a cocharacter mu over an algebraically closed coefficient field, the pointwise BB map on the good type-[mu] cell is bijective if all Ad(mu)-weights are ≤1. For the second assertion, let a group Gamma act on R preserving its maximal ideal; assume C^Gamma lies in the coefficient field, G and [mu] are defined over C^Gamma, and Gamma preserves the line (C^Gamma)·t and acts on it by an infinite-order character. Then the Gamma-fixed part of this good cell is exactly the canonical lifts of the C^Gamma-rational flags. In particular this applies to B_dR and the Galois action of a discretely valued p-adic K0⊂C with infinite cyclotomic extension. The fixed-point assertion concerns the good cell, not arbitrary lattices.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: For the weight-bound statement compute positive-loop root coordinates and their truncation degrees.
For Galois invariance apply the cyclotomic action on graded B_dR and eliminate negative non-invariant coefficients.
acceptance: An adjoint weight ≥2 leaves a nontrivial BB fibre; the assertion is not made for all lattices without the Galois hypothesis.

nodes.title: G-isocrystals and basic classes
nodes.statement: For connected linear G/Q_p, a G-isocrystal is an exact tensor functor Rep_Qp G→Isoc(Q_p-breve). Its isomorphism classes form B(G), equivalently sigma-conjugacy classes in G(Q_p-breve). Define its Newton homomorphism nu:D→G over Q_p-breve and call it basic when nu is central in G. Define B(G,[mu]) by the inverse image of B(M,[mu_M]) for the reductive Levi quotient M=G/R_uG.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Use Steinberg for the reductive quotient and successive split vector-group quotients for the unipotent radical.
Identify the representation functor of b with Frobenius rho(b) sigma.
Obtain Newton grading representationwise from Dieudonné–Manin.
acceptance: Basicness must be tested in G, not merely its Levi quotient.

nodes.title: Pointwise p-adic Hodge structures

nodes.statement: An admissible pair over C is a finite-dimensional isocrystal W/Q_p-breve together with a B_dR+-lattice L_et⊂W⊗B_dR such that the modified bundle E(W)_{L_et} is semistable of slope zero. nodes.title: Pointwise Tannakian theorems
nodes.statement: HS(C) and AdmPair(C) are Q_p-linear neutral Tannakian categories under the underlying V and V_et fibre functors. Their Tannakian fundamental groups are connected. The isocrystal fibre functor on admissible pairs is exact and faithful after extension to Q_p-breve. The full basic subcategory is tensor stable.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Compute saturated kernels and images in a fixed slope using degree inequalities.
Prove exactness and End(1)=Q_p, then apply neutral reconstruction.
Show an object with finite tensor monodromy is trivial, using the modification and the constant isocrystal, so the group has no nontrivial finite quotient.

nodes.title: Basic pairs and Hodge structures
nodes.statement: Étale realization gives a tensor equivalence between basic admissible pairs and Q-graded p-adic Hodge structures. The slope-nu piece of W corresponds to the weight-2nu piece of V_et with L_dR. Inverse construction recovers the slope-graded isocrystal from the modified pure bundles, together with L_et.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Use the slope grading respected by L_et to grade the étale realization.
Apply the pure bundle classification on each graded summand and invert the comparison.
Check tensor, dual, and the Tate convention.
acceptance: The weight is twice the isocrystal slope; the bundle functor reverses that slope.

nodes.title: Mumford–Tate and motivic Galois groups
nodes.statement: For a G-object in HS(C) or AdmPair(C), choose its indicated fibre trivialization and define MT or MG as tensor automorphisms of the fibre functor on the full tensor subcategory generated by the object, including subquotients. Construct its canonical reduction of structure group and characterize it by all tensor constructions and their Hodge/Tate lines, including nontrivial characters; weight-zero tensors alone need not suffice.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.

Apply reconstruction and the Chevalley line criterion.
Form the reduction via the tensor-isomorphism torsor and transport the chosen fibre trivialization.
acceptance: The reduction is minimal among subgroups supporting the full object, not only its individual representation fibres.

nodes.title: Invariants and existence
nodes.statement: For a good G-Hodge structure of type [mu] whose weight homomorphism is central in G (in particular after reduction to its Mumford–Tate group), its associated G-isocrystal is the unique basic class in B(G,[mu^-1]); its Newton homomorphism is half the weight homomorphism. For a good G-admissible pair the type and isocrystal class satisfy [b]∈B(G,[mu^-1]). Conversely every [b] in this set admits a G-admissible pair of that type over C, and one defined by a filtration over a suitable finite extension of Q_p-breve([mu]). A G-basic class must exist for the Hodge-structure assertion.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Read the Newton homomorphism from the weight grading.
Use the reductive admissibility condition and Levi reduction for necessity.

Use imported reductive rigid-point existence and lift along the unipotent filtration; at the resulting finite field of definition the Galois-fixed good lattice is the canonical lift of its rational trace flag by AP0 lattice_recovery.

nodes.title: Rigidified BKF comparison

nodes.title: Good reduction and analytic lattices
nodes.statement: Let C0=W(k_C)[1/p] inside C and let C0bar denote its algebraic closure inside C. An admissible pair has good reduction over a strict p-adic K⊂C if its lattice is the canonical lattice sum_i Fil^i B_dR·F^-i(W_K) of a K-filtration. Call a pair C0bar-analytic if it has good reduction over some finite K/C0. For a lattice in V⊗B_dR, analytic over a subfield means that it is the canonical lattice of a filtration over that subfield, with its specified rational structure. CM means that its connected MT/MG group is a torus.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.

acceptance: Analyticity is stronger than coordinates of a reduced flag alone for an arbitrary non-good lattice.

nodes.title: Crystalline realization of good reduction
nodes.statement: For strict p-adic K and C=completed algebraic closure of K, étale realization lifts to a fully faithful tensor functor AdmPair_good-red(K)→Rep_Qp Gal(Kbar/K). Its essential image is contained in the crystalline representations and is stable under subobjects. The B_cris invariants recover the filtered isocrystal and the B_dR comparison recovers the lattice. No non-strict-field version is asserted here.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.

Take B_cris invariants, recover W by slope classification over the strict field and recover L_et by the comparison.
Apply dimension inequalities to a stable subspace and its quotient.
acceptance: Full faithfulness and subobject stability both enter the identification of the algebraic Galois envelope.

nodes.title: Open Galois image
nodes.statement: For a G-admissible pair with good reduction over a strict p-adic field K and a chosen étale fibre trivialization, the continuous Galois representation has image open in MG(Q_p). Its Zariski closure equals MG. For a classical point initially defined over a non-strict discretely valued field F, base change to the completion of its maximal unramified extension F′; the restricted inertia image is open in the same geometric MG and supplies an open subgroup orbit contained in the original Galois orbit.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Identify the algebraic Galois envelope using full faithfulness and subobjects.
Apply Serre’s Hodge–Tate openness criterion in that envelope.
For F′ retain the same geometric pair and MG, then use inclusion of its Galois group into the original decomposition group.
acceptance: Use containment of an open subgroup orbit, not equality with the entire Galois orbit.

nodes.title: Two-lattice CM criterion
nodes.statement: Write C0=W(k_C)[1/p] and let C0bar be its algebraic closure inside C. For a basic admissible pair over C, having both its étale lattice (relative to W) and its de Rham lattice (relative to V_et) defined by filtrations over finite extensions of C0 is equivalent to having CM. In the CM case the étale lattice can be defined over Q_p-breve-bar and the de Rham lattice over Q_p-bar. Equivalently a good-reduction p-adic Hodge structure has C0bar-analytic de Rham lattice exactly when it has CM. For a C0bar-analytic admissible pair without basicness, if its de Rham lattice is also C0bar-analytic, the slope filtration lifts to subpairs and its graded subpairs have CM; the original extension need not split or have CM.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Reduce the CM direction to a torus; its flag varieties are points, so the character/cocharacter lattice description makes both filtrations algebraic over the stated smaller fields.
For the converse the algebraic filtration has an open MG orbit fixed by its field of definition, forcing central cocharacters and then a torus.
In the nonbasic case use the lifted slope filtration and apply the basic statement to each graded part.
acceptance: The nonbasic refinement yields CM graded pieces, not a semisimplicity or splitting assertion.

nodes.title: Rigid analytic subdiamonds
nodes.statement: Fix a complete nonarchimedean field L. Use the rigid analytic points supplied by RZ.3 (finite-extension-valued points over L). A rigid analytic diamond is one isomorphic over Spd L to S^diamond for a seminormal rigid analytic L-variety S. A rigid analytic subdiamond is a locally closed subdiamond represented in this way; a closed rigid analytic subdiamond also has closed immersion into the ambient diamond. These notions retain the field of definition.

nodes.title: Coefficient and group local systems
nodes.statement: For a locally spatial diamond Y, a Λ-local system (Λ a complete Huber ring) is a sheaf on Y_v which is v-locally finite free over the sheaf of continuous Λ-valued functions. For B=O, B_dR+ or B_dR use finite locally free sheaves of B-modules on Y_v. For a complete Huber Q_p-algebra Λ, a G-local system is an exact tensor functor Rep_Qp G→Loc_Λ(Y), equivalently its v-local tensor-frame torsor. An O-local system is an analytic vector bundle exactly when it is étale-locally trivial as an O-local system; every O-local system on a perfectoid space has this property, whereas a general rigid variety has additional O-local systems. The pro-étale description of Q_p-local systems is used only under its proved comparison hypotheses.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Use v-descent for finite projective modules and continuous coefficient functions.
Construct tensor frames v-locally and apply the tensor-isomorphism torsor theorem.
For Q_p use the stated pro-étale comparison; for O use the étale-trivializability criterion, rather than identifying all rigid v-local systems with analytic bundles.

For the affinoid B_dR+ comparison use the existing completed-period bundle v-descent. For B_dR use the explicitly requested localized-period finite-projective descent extension; O-module descent alone does not prove this case.
acceptance: Local freeness and its topology are part of the object; a sheaf with merely finite-dimensional fibres is insufficient.

nodes.title: Closed integrality locus
nodes.statement: Let L be a p-adic field, S an affinoid perfectoid space over L, X an affine finite-type L-scheme, and x∈X(B_dR(S)). The subset of |S| where every geometric specialization of x lies in X(B_dR+) is Zariski closed. Integrality is functorial under morphisms of affine finite-type L-schemes. Zariski closedness is transitive for the associated closed perfectoid subspaces.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Choose a closed immersion X→A^n_L and test its finitely many coordinates.
Bound their denominators locally and successively kill negative filtration coefficients; each obstruction is a section of a Tate-twisted O-line and has a Zariski closed zero locus.

For transitivity identify a closed perfectoid subspace with its strong closed quotient. Surjectivity of the quotient map lifts defining ideals, so successive zero loci are cut out by one ideal upstairs.
acceptance: The bound is finite for each coordinate; no globally preferred generator t is imposed.

nodes.title: Relative bilattices and their type
nodes.statement: A bilatticed B_dR-local system on Y is (V,L1,L2), with V a B_dR-local system and Li B_dR+-local systems identified with lattices in V. A latticed B_dR+-local system is equivalently (L1,L2⊂L1[1/Fil^1]); the datum is not merely a G(B_dR+)-local system with one lattice. Define trace filtrations by image of Fil^i B_dR·L2∩L1 in L1/Fil^1L1, and type pointwise by elementary divisors. A filtered O-local system uses locally direct summands and a pointwise-locally-constant rank function.

proofSteps: Sheafify intersection and image and compare on strictly totally disconnected presentations.
Identify geometric fibres with pointwise bilattices.
For locally constant type prove the trace terms locally split and compute the two graded pieces.
acceptance: Type need not be locally constant in an arbitrary family.

nodes.title: Relative goodness and trace exactness
nodes.statement: A bilatticed G-local system is good of locally constant type [mu] iff BB1 is a filtered G(O)-local system of type [mu^-1], iff BB2 is one of type [mu]. This is HK II Theorem 3.2.1. For reductive G, type satisfies the usual Schubert semicontinuity; no such general assertion is made for non-reductive G.

nodes.title: The trivial-filtration lattice functor
nodes.statement: For smooth rigid X over a p-adic field L, define M0(E,∇) as Scholze’s B_dR+-local system attached to the flat bundle with trivial filtration. It is a fully faithful tensor functor from flat bundles on X_et; There is a canonical residual comparison M0(E)⊗O≅v^*E, and pushing forward recovers E with its connection. For a Griffiths-transversal filtration F on E define M(E,F)⊂M0(E)[1/Fil^1] by the filtered de Rham horizontal-section construction, giving the associated latticed object.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Use the local Poincaré lemma and the horizontal-section construction.
Compute the pushforward locally in toric coordinates.
Descend and compare tensor products and strict morphisms.
acceptance: M0 takes a flat bundle as input; it forgets any pre-existing filtration.

nodes.title: Smooth rigid lattice–filtration comparison
nodes.statement: For smooth rigid X over a p-adic field L, the functor (E,∇,F)↦(M0(E),M(E,F)) is fully faithful on Griffiths-transversal filtered flat bundles. Its essential image is exactly the latticed objects whose first lattice is M0 of a flat bundle and whose trace filtration has locally direct-summand terms (equivalently locally constant type). The recovered filtration is on X_et, not only on its pro-étale cover.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Use the residual comparison M0(E)⊗O≅v^*E. On an analytic open U trivializing E, the trace direct summands define U^diamond→Flag, not merely a map from a pro-étale chart.
Apply seminormal rigid full faithfulness to U and its overlap opens; uniqueness glues the analytic filtration on E.
The Faltings-extension boundary, or induction on the filtration spread as in HK II §3.3, identifies vanishing of the lattice lifting obstruction with Griffiths transversality.
Apply the associated-lattice position and uniqueness theorem to recover the original second lattice; horizontal full faithfulness gives the morphism assertion.
acceptance: Smoothness is required here. Singular applications use AP5 rigid_cells and resolution instead.

sources.locator: arXiv v2, Theorem 3.3.1(3), pp. 24–25; Proposition 5.0.3(4), p. 31
sources.match: The essential-image argument requires analytic descent of the flag. The residual comparison of the first lattice produces an actual map from each analytic trivializing open to a rigid flag variety; seminormal full faithfulness then applies. The Faltings extension detects Griffiths transversality.

nodes.title: Non-reductive de Rham Grassmannians
nodes.statement: For connected linear G/Q_p, Gr_G is the étale sheaf quotient G(B_dR)/G(B_dR+), equivalently G(B_dR+)-torsors with a trivialization after inverting Fil^1. It is a v-sheaf. For a cocharacter class [mu], Gr_[mu] is the good lattice locus of type [mu] and BB:Gr_[mu]→Fl_[mu^-1]^diamond is the first trace-filtration map. Define Fl as filtrations of the standard fibre functor; its type components are clopen and descend to their reflex fields.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Use tensor torsors and effective coefficient-module descent.
Extend the reductive quotient description through the unipotent derived series.
On geometric points use the good double-coset condition and descend the trace flag.
acceptance: A non-reductive Grassmannian need not be the union of its good cocharacter cells.

nodes.title: Subgroup immersion criterion
nodes.statement: For a closed embedding H→G of connected linear groups, Gr_H→Gr_G is a monomorphism. It is locally closed if G/H is quasi-affine, and closed if G/H is affine. Prove these statements by integral loci in an observable embedding, not by assuming every faithful representation gives a closed Grassmannian embedding.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Express a reduction to H as an integral section of the homogeneous-space model.
Use a Chevalley line and its inverse-character G_m factor to obtain an observable embedding.
Apply the closed-integrality lemma for affine quotients, and its open restriction for quasi-affine ones.
acceptance: The affineness and quasi-affineness hypotheses are kept distinct.

nodes.title: Grassmannian geometry and Schubert loci
nodes.statement: For connected linear G, Gr_G is separated, partially proper and an increasing union of closed locally spatial diamonds. Every Gr_[mu] is locally closed; it is closed in Gr_G if [mu_M] is minuscule for the reductive Levi quotient. For any [mu], Gr_[mu] is closed in Gr_G×_{Gr_M}Gr_[mu_M].
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Embed G observably into GL(V)×G_m and import reductive bounded diamonds.
Use Levi-cell local closedness.
In its Levi preimage cut out the required cell by the faithful-representation dominance bound of specialization.
Apply the valuative criterion for partial properness with the same embeddings.
acceptance: Do not strengthen local closedness to closedness for an arbitrary cocharacter.

nodes.title: Faithful-representation cutout
nodes.statement: Fix a Levi G=M⋉U and a closed faithful rho:G→GL(V). In Gr_G×_{Gr_M}Gr_[mu_M], the cell Gr_[mu] is exactly the inverse image under rho of the closed Schubert bound Gr_GL(V),≤rho(mu). Thus Gr_[mu]=(Gr_G×_{Gr_M}Gr_[mu_M])∩rho^-1(Gr_≤rho(mu)). The order is the usual reductive dominance order with matching determinant/Kottwitz invariant.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Specialization puts every actual representation type above the induced Levi type.
The imposed upper bound forces equality.
Faithfulness then forces goodness, proving the functorial equality on geometric points and the represented closed subdiamond.
acceptance: Both the Levi-type condition and the representation bound are necessary.

nodes.title: Rigid sources and Griffiths transversality
nodes.statement: For a seminormal rigid S/L and a map S^diamond→Gr_G whose Levi projection lands in Gr_[mu_M], the map factors through Gr_[mu]. BB identifies such maps with filtrations of type [mu^-1] on the trivial G-bundle whose restriction to the smooth locus is Griffiths transversal for the trivial connection. For smooth S the condition holds everywhere. Every rigid analytic point of Gr_G is good. No claim is made that all geometric points are good.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: At a classical point use the infinite cyclotomic Galois action to recover a canonical lattice.
The closed cutout and density give the factorization.
On a resolution use the smooth comparison of AP4.
Descend the flag and its canonical lattice along the resolution and its fibre product by seminormal full faithfulness.
acceptance: This replaces each invalid use of the smooth theorem on a singular base.

nodes.title: Adjoint-weight BB criterion
nodes.statement: BB:Gr_[mu]→Fl_[mu^-1]^diamond is an isomorphism iff all weights of Ad∘mu on Lie G are ≤1. If any weight exceeds 1, BB has no section over any nonempty open subdiamond of the flag variety. For reductive G this condition is equivalent to minuscule [mu]; for non-reductive G it is a one-sided bound. In particular every rigid analytic map into Gr_Ga is zero, although Gr_Ga has many geometric points.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Compute the congruence stabilizer of t^mu in each adjoint weight.
For the bounded case identify the quotient with the flag.
For the converse a hypothetical section yields a filtration with impossible Griffiths-transverse differential in a weight >1 direction.
acceptance: Replacing ≤1 by |weight|≤1 for general G loses legitimate one-sided examples.

nodes.title: Neutral admissible pairs in families
nodes.statement: For a nonempty locally spatial Y/Spd Q_p-breve, a neutral admissible pair is a fixed finite-dimensional isocrystal W together with a B_dR+-lattice L_et⊂W⊗B_dR whose geometric fibres are admissible. W is globally constant, including on disconnected Y. Morphisms are fixed isocrystal maps preserving the lattice. Define omega_et by the slope-zero bundle/local-system equivalence, c_dR by modification, omega_Isoc=W, and L_dR=c_dR^-1(W⊗B_dR+).

Recover the two lattices using the same comparison isomorphism.
acceptance: Do not replace the fixed isocrystal by an arbitrary isocrystal local system.

nodes.statement: For nonempty locally spatial Y/Spd Q_p-breve, neutral admissible pairs form a Q_p-linear neutral Tannakian category; evaluation of omega_et at any geometric y is an exact faithful fibre functor. The underlying isocrystal functor is exact and faithful. Prove kernels, images and cokernels as families, using local triviality of constant-slope bundles rather than inferring it from pointwise rank alone. This is HK II Theorem 7.1.2.

Use exactness in each point category and the relative constant-slope/local-system theorem to show the lattices are locally free of the required ranks.
Check End(1)=Q_p; a single fibre detects a fixed isocrystal map.
acceptance: The evaluation remains faithful even for disconnected Y because the isocrystal maps are fixed.

nodes.title: G-families and canonical reduction
nodes.statement: A neutral G-admissible pair is an exact tensor functor A:Rep_Qp G→AdmPair^neutral(Y) such that, at every geometric y, omega_y∘A is isomorphic to the standard fibre functor. These isomorphisms are required to exist, not chosen as part of the object. With a chosen geometric fibre trivialization define H=MG(A,y)≤G from its generated tensor subcategory. H is connected. The isocrystal tensor functor of its canonical H-reduction is globally fixed and is isomorphic to W_bH for some b_H∈H(Q_p-breve), without a connectedness hypothesis. If Y is connected, its étale fibre functors all have the standard H-form, so the reduction is neutral. With g sending f(b_H) to b by sigma-conjugation, the classifying map factors through the H-admissible locus. For disconnected Y this assertion is made componentwise, not with one universal neutral reduction.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: A finite tensor quotient is trivial at every geometric point by the pointwise connectedness theorem. Its constant isocrystal maps then preserve the lattices globally, proving connectedness of MG.
The H-isocrystal functor is already fixed globally. Steinberg triviality over Q_p-breve gives b_H and a sigma-conjugating g, independently of connectedness of Y.
The form of the étale H-fibre functor lies in ker(H^1(Q_p,H)→H^1(Q_p,G)). A continuous H-torsor has locally constant fibre form; on connected Y the form is fixed by its standard value at y.
Use this neutrality and g to obtain the H-admissible factorization. On a disconnected base another component can have a different étale form.
acceptance: Connectedness of MG and neutrality of the reduction are separate obligations.

nodes.title: Good type over rigid bases
nodes.statement: Let S be a geometrically connected seminormal rigid analytic variety over a p-adic L⊇Q_p-breve, and let A be a neutral G-admissible pair on S^diamond. Then its bilatticed G-local system is good and has a single type [mu], with [mu] defined over L. For connected S not geometrically connected, pass to its finite field of constants and apply the statement componentwise. For a connected seminormal S whose classifying map has fixed ambient type, the canonical motivic reduction also has a fixed subgroup type after the appropriate reflex-field extension.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Descend the Q_p-local system to the étale site and resolve the seminormal rigid source; the resolution is a proper surjective v-cover.

On the smooth source the de Rham comparison identifies L_et⊗OB_dR with W_L⊗OB_dR for the constant flat bundle W_L. Invoke the explicitly requested full-rank de Rham criterion over arbitrary p-adic L; this criterion is a recorded supplier gap, not an application of finite-field Liu–Zhu rigidity.

That criterion gives the associated locally split Griffiths-transversal filtration, hence goodness and locally constant type. Geometric connectedness and Galois descent make its conjugacy class single and L-defined.
Use rigid_cells only after the Levi type is known: it lifts that type to G. Uniqueness on analytic trivializations and seminormal full faithfulness descend the filtration from the resolution.
Apply the same argument to the canonical motivic subgroup after the connected-base neutral reduction. General rigid sources factor through their seminormalizations at the diamond level.
acceptance: Do not apply Liu–Zhu’s finite-Q_p-field rigidity theorem directly over an arbitrary strict field or singular S.
The arbitrary-field full-rank criterion is an explicit open input. A fixed-type Grassmannian theorem cannot establish its own type hypothesis.

The plan replaces this appeal with a precise independent supplier criterion and records the missing verification; the fixed-Levi-type theorem is used only after constancy is obtained.

Pull back the open trivial bundle stratum.
Recover a b-rigidified pair from its lattice and prove the representing equivalence functorially.
acceptance: The entire admissible locus may contain points outside every good type cell for non-reductive G.

nodes.title: Cohomologically smooth connected products
nodes.statement: Let C/Q_p be complete algebraically closed, let ℓ≠p, and let X and Y be nonempty connected locally spatial diamonds which are ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spd C. Then X×_(Spd C)Y is connected. Cohomological smoothness includes separatedness, compactifiability and local finiteness of dim.trg for the structure maps.

nodes.title: Neutral Hodge structures in families
nodes.statement: For nonempty locally spatial Y/Spd Q_p-breve, a neutral p-adic Hodge structure is a fixed finite Q-graded Q_p-space V and a B_dR+-lattice L_dR in V⊗B_dR, compatible with grading and having pointwise Hodge-structure fibres of the prescribed weights. Morphisms are fixed graded Q_p-linear maps preserving L_dR. A G-structure is an exact tensor functor into this category; its MT group at y is defined from the generated tensor subcategory. For a G-structure require its fixed étale tensor functor to be isomorphic to the standard fibre functor. A choice of that isomorphism is the additional trivialization used by the represented domain.

nodes.title: The Hodge period domain
nodes.statement: Fix a connected linear G and [mu] for which B(G,[mu^-1]) has a G-basic class. Let X_[mu]⊂Gr_[mu^-1] be the open locus where the modified trivial bundle is basic. Its geometric connectedness is proved in AP9 after basic duality.

nodes.title: Special Hodge subvarieties
nodes.statement: For connected H≤G and type [mu_H] inducing [mu_G], with a basic class for H whose image in B(G) is the ambient G-basic class, the map X_[mu_H]→X_[mu_G] is the subgroup period map. nodes.title: Borel and parabolic boundary examples
nodes.statement: Let H be the upper triangular Borel of G=GL_2, and let mu_G(t)=diag(t^-1,1). Write L_[a:c]=R^2+R xi^-1(a e1+c e2). For b=diag(p,1), G-admissibility means a≠0, whereas H-admissibility in the full preimage means c=0. Thus a c≠0 gives an ambient-admissible point that is not subgroup-admissible. With b=diag(1,p), the particular H-cell <e1,xi^-1(e2+x e1)> is A^1 and maps isomorphically to the G-admissible part P^1 minus [e1]; both loci are H-admissible there. Separately, for G=GL_3 and H stabilizing the span of e1,e2, the family <e1,e2+(z/xi)e1,e3+(1/xi)e1> has constant G-type (1,0,−1); its GL_2×GL_1 Levi type is (1,−1;0) for z≠0 and (0,0;0) at z=0. Therefore a subgroup cell can fail to be closed in an ambient fixed-type cell, and subgroup Schubert decompositions need not be intersections with ambient cells.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Compute elementary divisors and induced Levi lattices in the displayed bases.
Separate G-triviality of the modified bundle from the H-fibre-functor neutrality condition.
Compare the nonzero-z locus with its limit at zero.
acceptance: The Borel’s b is diag(1,p) for the A^1 assertion; the reversed diagonal describes a different example.

nodes.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected linear, [mu] a cocharacter class admitting a G-basic [b]∈B(G,[mu^-1]), choose b and let M=M_{b,[mu]}. nodes.title: Variations of p-adic Hodge structure
nodes.statement: For smooth rigid S/L, a variation of p-adic Hodge structure is a finite Q-graded de Rham Q_p-local system L=⊕L_lambda for which each fibre (L_lambda,M0,lambda) is a weight-lambda p-adic Hodge structure. Here M0 is the lattice from the trivial filtration on the associated flat bundle, while the original local system determines the étale rational structure. A G-variation is an exact tensor functor Rep_Qp G into this category. A pro-étale K-torsor for open K≤G(Q_p) is de Rham if its associated representation local systems are de Rham, equivalently for one closed faithful representation.

Impose the pure bundle condition on each graded fibre.
acceptance: The Q_p-local system is allowed to have monodromy here; this is a distinct family notion from the neutral category.

nodes.title: Katz–Igusa obstruction
nodes.statement: On the ordinary locus of a connected finite-level modular curve without p-level, the Katz–Igusa Z_p×-tower trivializing the unit-root isocrystal equals the crystalline-frame cover for the associated rank-one de Rham torsor. Its surjective infinite Z_p× monodromy prevents refinement by a rigid analytic de Jong cover of the asserted kind; its inverse-limit adic realization is not a finite-type rigid analytic variety.
hypotheses: The coefficient, group, field, base and type hypotheses are those explicitly quantified in this statement; the conventions fix all filtration and slope signs.
proofSteps: Import the ordinary Katz–Igusa formal tower, its geometric connectedness and its Z_p×-monodromy from the precise Igusa supplier request. It is not supplied by the Hodge-type perfectoid-tower theorem.
Compare the rank-one crystalline realization with the unit-root factor in the matching covariant or dual Tate normalization; this identifies the frame cover with the Katz–Igusa tower.

A reduction to a rigid de Jong covering forces the corresponding compact fibre monodromy to have finite orbits, contradicting the infinite transitive Z_p× action. Non-finite-type inverse limits do not provide a rigid variety.
acceptance: This example is a boundary to rigid refinement, not a disproof of the potentially unramified expectation.

nodes.title: Products of Shimura curves
nodes.statement: Let D/Q be a quaternion algebra split at infinity and ramified at p, with neat level away from p and maximal local level; let B be the inner form definite at infinity and split at p. For a product of n associated curves over Q_p-breve, each chosen component has a Čerednik–Drinfeld presentation Omega^n/Gamma, with Gamma the product of the arithmetic component stabilizers. After base change to C, at infinite level the local product M of Drinfeld spaces and the global perfectoid tower have compatible Hodge–Tate maps and differ by the corresponding arithmetic quotient. Locally in the analytic topology this is the local period diagram. Thus the opposite analytic closure of a lifted irreducible analytic set is the transported image of the appropriate local special subvariety.

Form the product diagram and the compatible perfectoid inverse levels.
Proper discontinuity makes the finite-level uniformization analytic-locally an isomorphism.
Transport AP11 through that diagram; the bi-algebraic Chambert-Loir–Loeser theorem concerns a different pair of algebraic structures and is comparison context, not an input to this implication.

Both trace filtrations use the same invertible period ideal. The jumping-type disc is not a filtered local system by direct summands; exact period-ring inputs retained.
The relative tensor-exactness criterion is v-local and geometric-fibrewise. It does not assume that arbitrary families have constant type.
Strengthened residual recovery to M0(E) tensor O = pullback E, with connection recovered by pushforward. This justifies the analytic trivializations used for flag descent.
Supplied the missing analytic descent argument using local analytic trivializations of E and seminormal full faithfulness, with the Faltings extension enforcing transversality.
The non-reductive extension imports the existing reductive Grassmannian, preserves fpqc sheafification and distinguishes many geometric G_a points from its single rigid-source image.
The observable/affine quotient hypotheses are retained. A subgroup map is not declared closed solely because it is a group embedding.
The geometric and relative-position assertions use the exact reductive Schubert, bundle and rigid-source inputs; the non-reductive extension remains owned here.
Finite tensor conditions for a closed faithful representation detect the G-lattice condition; exact tensor gluing inputs supply the ambient comparison.
Theorem 5.0.4(4) keeps its fixed Levi-type hypothesis. Resolution and seminormal descent do not establish that hypothesis; AP6 now records the separate criterion.
The upper adjoint bound alone characterizes the first BB isomorphism. The inverse type uses the opposite bound; the non-reductive example separates them.
The fixed W is global even on a disconnected base. Exact relative slope-zero and HN inputs replace the old broad supplier request.

Removed the circular fixed-type argument. The arbitrary-field full-rank de Rham criterion is an explicit independent P8 request and gap; the target is justified as a source theorem conditional on that input.

The line is a rank-one sub-isocrystal with its own slope and Tate normalization. Ambient admissibility does not automatically make it an admissible subobject.
